title: Rugiet reviews and cost: comparison with FutureClinic - FutureClinic
summary: Rugiet reviews, cost and legitimacy: what is in Rugiet Ready, BBB ratings, subscription rules, and how FDA-approved ED generics compare.
body_markdown:
## Rugiet vs an FDA-approved generic from a FutureClinic doctor


Rugiet Generic from a FutureClinic doctor


What you get Compounded blends like Ready A physician and, if right for you, an FDA-approved generic


Who prescribes "Board-certified physicians"; partner consent includes nurses Physicians only (MD, DO or MBBS)


Price $79/mo for 6 doses (landing page, Nov 2026); $7.29 to $19.96 a dose (Rugiet's blog prices, verified June 2026) Visit: $40 (best-fit) or $20 to $100. Tadalafil 5 mg (30): $5.97 + $5.25 shipping (Cost Plus Drugs, Nov 2026)


Subscription 30- or 90-day auto-refill; you can opt in or out of a membership plan No subscription required


Where it's filled Partner pharmacies only The pharmacy you choose


FDA-approved product No (compounded) Yes


Prices checked on November 3, 2026.


Monthly plans assume you stay subscribed to keep getting refills, while one FutureClinic visit can cover several months of a stable prescription when your doctor judges it safe. Rugiet's "$79/mo (6 doses)" landing-page plan (November 2026) is $948 a year, or about $525 for 72 doses at the about $7.29 quarterly price in Rugiet's blog (verified June 2026). A $40 FutureClinic visit plus 90 generic sildenafil 100 mg tablets at[Cost Plus Drugs](https://api.costplusdrugs.com/pricelist/cpd) ($10.07 plus $5.25 shipping, November 2026) is about $55, if your doctor decides it's right for you. Cost Plus Drugs lists 30 tablets of tadalafil 5 mg at $5.97 and sildenafil 100 mg at $6.69 (plus $5.25 shipping),[GoodRx](https://www.goodrx.com/sildenafil) coupons run $13.70 for[tadalafil 5 mg](https://www.goodrx.com/tadalafil) (30 tablets) to $15.37 for sildenafil 100 mg (10 tablets) (November 2026), and insurance may cover the medicine.


## Who should pick Rugiet


Rugiet suits men who specifically want its compounded formula, such as Rugiet Ready (sildenafil, tadalafil and apomorphine, dissolved under the tongue), or its other blends. It also fits someone who wants the consultation, compounded medicine from Rugiet's partner pharmacies and follow-ups priced into one 30-day or 90-day bill. FutureClinic has no proprietary combination or compounded product of its own. FutureClinic sends prescriptions only to the pharmacy you choose and never sells or bundles the medicine.


## Why a doctor of your own and a generic you can fill anywhere


Ask yourself: do you want a company's compounded blend with its subscription billing and partner-pharmacy rules, or did you want one-to-one access to a doctor of your own and an FDA-approved generic you can fill anywhere? If you want what Rugiet sells beyond the doctor visit, it is a strong option. If you wanted an expert physician, FutureClinic gives you that with nothing attached.


Every FutureClinic doctor is a licensed physician (MD, DO or MBBS), never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant. A specific doctor reads your whole case and answers with a Human Signature, a short video or voice note recorded live for you. No form is approved in bulk. Replies take hours, not minutes: typically the same day. Visits cost $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100.


The[AUA](https://www.auanet.org/guidelines-and-quality/guidelines/erectile-dysfunction-(ed)-guideline) notes ED is a cardiovascular risk marker, and the[NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/erectile-dysfunction/symptoms-causes) links it to diabetes, high blood pressure and low testosterone. Your physician can order morning testosterone labs and check interactions (nitrates and riociguat are contraindicated per the[sildenafil](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?query=viagra) and[tadalafil](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?query=cialis) labels). FutureClinic doctors do not prescribe controlled substances, including testosterone. Seek emergency care for an erection over 4 hours or sudden vision or hearing loss ([sildenafil label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?query=viagra) ).


To adjust doses or switch medicines, you message the same doctor in one chat, who can also treat other problems in their specialty. FutureClinic has over 300 doctors. You can see generalists and specialists across more than 60 specialties, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record. Doctors earn nothing extra for any prescription or test, and no subscription is required, though most offer an optional membership (unlimited care with that doctor, typically $25 to $100 a month, cancel any time).


## How to talk to a doctor about ED on FutureClinic


Visit[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) to start a conversation with a doctor right away, or you can even do it from your AI app. Connect ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex or Grok Bot at[futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) or send:` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt` . Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.


When a prescription goes to the pharmacy you choose, a text brings a discount coupon for the best cash price. FutureClinic works in 34 states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. Your doctor must be licensed in your state; if you do not see your state here, try anyway because FutureClinic may have opened there since. FutureClinic is not for emergencies: call 911 in an emergency, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.
